facts.claim: Titles can be up to 100 characters.
Descriptions can be up to 5,000 characters.
With more than 15 hashtags on a video, YouTube ignores all of them.
Square or vertical videos up to three minutes can be Shorts.
facts.note: Secondary source. Confirm in YouTube Help before you plan around the exact limit.

facts.claim: Shorts analytics show 'How many chose to view': the share of times people watched rather than swiped away.
facts.note: The only response metric the source attributes to YouTube's own documentation. Use it as your first Shorts hook metric.

facts.claim: A Short 'engaged view' is described as clicking to watch or watching past the initial seconds.
facts.primary: YouTube blog (the page dates it Aug 2026)
facts.note: Dating on the secondary source is inconsistent. Treat as unconfirmed.

facts.claim: From 1 Oct 2026 YouTube says it is updating its systems to further prioritize original content, which reduces reach for re-uploads that add nothing of the creator's own.
facts.note: Do not re-upload other people's clips. Add commentary, analysis or new footage.

facts.claim: YouTube Studio's Test & compare can test thumbnails, and since July 2025 titles too.
facts.note: Availability can differ by channel. Check Studio.

facts.claim: YouTube has not published its ranking signals or their weights. What you control is packaging and retention.
facts.note: Anyone quoting exact weights is guessing.

facts.claim: Captions can be up to 2,200 characters.
Instagram caps hashtags at five per post.
facts.note: Reported as effective December 2025. Confirm in the Instagram Help Center.

facts.claim: Reels can be up to three minutes.
Adam Mosseri named watch time, likes per reach and sends per reach as the top ranking signals for video.
facts.source: PostEverywhere citing Social Media Today, Jan 2025
facts.note: Rates matter more than counts. Sends per reach is the one to watch.

facts.claim: Mosseri said he would not think of hashtags as a way to get more distribution.
As of April 2026, Instagram no longer recommends accounts that regularly repost content they did not create, now including photos and carousels.
Roughly the first 125 characters of a caption show before 'more'.
facts.note: Treat as a rule of thumb. Test on your own phone.

facts.claim: 'Your Algorithm' lets people tune Reels recommendations. Launched for Reels in the US in December 2025.
TikTok's explainers list interactions (watch time, completion, replays, likes, comments, shares, follows, 'not interested'), video information and user or device settings. Weights are not published.
Search is described as using caption keywords, hashtags, on-screen text and spoken words.
facts.note: Not attributed to TikTok. Put the keyword in what you say, in the on-screen text and in the caption.

facts.claim: Commonly advised length is 10 to 60 seconds, up to 180 in some niches.
facts.note: No TikTok source. Let retention decide.

facts.claim: Third-party analyses claim 75 to 100 percent completion triggers aggressive distribution.
facts.note: Not stated by TikTok. Useful as direction, not as a target.

facts.claim: TikTok requires realistic AI-generated content to be labelled and applies its own AI labels.
Meta says it will preferentially promote content filmed or produced directly by the creator or page owner.
facts.note: Remixes with real added analysis can qualify. Simple clips, stitches and light reactions are likely to be demoted.

facts.claim: Meta is testing a 1 to 5 interest-match survey after Reels. Low ratings count as negative even when watch time is high.
facts.note: In testing. Stay on-niche.

facts.claim: Meta reported Facebook Reels views and time spent roughly doubled in the second half of 2025 versus 2024.
Posts can be up to 3,000 characters.
Early engagement, comment depth and dwell time are widely modelled as ranking inputs. LinkedIn has not published weights.
facts.note: Metricool's model, not a LinkedIn statement.

facts.claim: Metricool's study of 600,000+ posts found carousels drew about 17x the interactions of images.
facts.note: Correlation. Images were also posted far more often. Not a ranking rule.

facts.claim: Standard posts are 280 characters. Premium accounts can write much longer posts (up to 25,000).

X published its For You ranking code in August 2026 (xai-org, Apache 2.0). Reported weights: reply, quote and DM share 5, copy-link about 20, follow 4, repost 1, like 0.5. Negative signals (report, mute, not interested, block) weigh far more. Weights apply to predicted probabilities, not raw counts. Posts older than 48 hours are filtered.
facts.primary: Published code, as relayed by Business Insider
facts.note: Read the code yourself before building strategy on a single number.

facts.claim: Posts can be up to 500 characters.
Between April and October 2026, YouTube, Instagram and Facebook each announced changes that favor original content over reposts.
facts.source: Our summary of three entries: youtube.originality.2026_10, instagram.originality.2026_04, facebook.original.2026_04
facts.note: Each platform entry carries its own source link. Design for it: your own footage, your own commentary, your own angle.

facts.claim: US FTC rules require a clear disclosure of any material connection to a brand, such as payment or free product.
facts.source: FTC, Disclosures 101 for social media influencers

facts.claim: In India, ASCI's influencer guidelines require a visible disclosure label when content is a paid or otherwise incentivised promotion.
facts.note: Check the current ASCI text for exact label wording.

facts.claim: In the EU, hiding the commercial nature of content is a prohibited unfair commercial practice.
YouTube requires creators to disclose realistic AI-generated or altered content, using the AI use setting (Yes or No) when uploading in YouTube Studio.
facts.source: YouTube Help, Disclosing use of altered or synthetic content

facts.claim: Instagram's branded content policies require the paid partnership label to tag the featured brand.
facts.source: Instagram Help, paid partnership label for organic branded content

facts.claim: ChatGPT and Codex load Agent Skills (SKILL.md). Uploading a ZIP works through Plugins > Skills > Create > Upload on paid plans except Free and Go; Enterprise and Edu need an admin to turn Skills on. Codex reads folder-based skills on every plan.
facts.note: UI names can change. If the menu differs, search the help center for 'skills'.

facts.claim: ChatGPT custom MCP connectors are set up under Settings > Connectors > Advanced > Developer Mode (beta), then Create with a remote MCP server URL.
facts.note: Needs a public HTTPS URL. A local server needs a tunnel.

facts.claim: SKILL.md frontmatter: name (up to 64 characters, lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens) and description (up to 1,024 characters) are required. license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools are optional. Keep the body under roughly 5,000 tokens.
Cursor loads Agent Skills from .agents/skills and .cursor/skills in a project, and ~/.agents/skills and ~/.cursor/skills for the user. It also loads .claude/skills and .codex/skills.
Gemini CLI discovers skills in .gemini/skills and .agents/skills (workspace) and ~/.gemini/skills and ~/.agents/skills (user). `gemini skills install <git url>` installs from a repository.

vidIQ says its MCP connector works with Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor on every plan including Free. Showrunner is not affiliated with vidIQ. If you connect it, the conductor can use its keyword and competitor data.
facts.note: Vendor claim from their site. Verify in your account.
